web.title: Same-sex marriage
web.description:
As of 2026,[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Same-sex_marriage&action=edit) marriage between [same-sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality) couples is legally performed and recognized in 38 countries, with a total population of 1.5 billion people (20% of the world's population). Same-sex marriage is legally recognized in a majority of the world's [developed countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developed_country) and across much of the [Western world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world). [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage#cite_note-15) A few of these are among the 35 countries (as of 2023) that constitutionally define marriage to prevent marriage between couples of the same sex, with most of those provisions enacted in recent decades as a preventative measure. ## History ### Contemporary [[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage#cite_note-bloomberg-2014-12-04-24)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage#cite_note-69) Since then, same-sex marriage has been established by law in 38 other countries, including most of the [Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americas) and [Western Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe). ## Same-sex marriage around the world Same-sex marriage is legally performed and recognized in 38 countries: [Andorra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Andorra), [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Argentina), web.title: Countries Where Gay Marriage Is Legal 2026
web.description:
# Countries Where Gay Marriage Is Legal 2026
### Gay Marriage Legal
40countries

Not every country in the world is involved in the conversation surrounding gay marriage, but a large percentage of the world’s nations have either legalized same-sex marriage, permitted gay marriage in certain parts of the country, allows civil unions between individuals of the same sex, or actively restricts gay marriage.

The number of countries that do not recognize same-sex couples are married, but rather, as having civil unions and partnerships, amounts to eleven nations.

# Our Blog
As of January 2025, same-sex marriage is legalised in 38 nations.

The list of countries to legalise same-sex marriage includes: Andorra, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Denmark, Ecuador, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and Uruguay.

Currently, Japan is the only G-7 nation that has yet to recognise same-sex civil unions or same-sex marriage.
